request: Analyze GSE244401 for the paper (Whole-Blood Transcriptome Analysis Reveals Distinct Gene Expression Signatures in Pediatric Patients with Sickle Cell Anemia Before and After Exercise): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: whole-blood bulk RNA-seq (PAXgene, polyA, NovaSeq), HISAT2 + featureCounts raw counts, GRCh38 (S2.3.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: 23 pediatric SCA (HbSS or S/beta0) and 17 age/ethnicity-matched healthy controls with valid RNA-seq both pre and post exercise (S2.1.p1, S3.p1, TAB1); 80 samples

factors.exercise_intensity: 50% vs 70% peak workload, pooled by the authors (S2.4.p1)

final.repeated_measure_unit: participant (pre and post blood draw from the same child, S2.3.p1); the paper does not state how within-subject correlation was modelled
final.primary_estimand: acute exercise effect (post vs pre) on whole-blood gene expression within SCA and within controls, and the group x time interaction (difference of the exercise response SCA vs CON)
planned_contrasts: post vs pre within SCA (S3.p1; paper: 391 up + 133 down = 524, P<0.01; Supp Table S2)
post vs pre within CON (S3.p1; paper: 333 up + 290 down = 623, P<0.01; Supp Table S3)
group x time interaction (S2.4.p1, S3.p1; paper: 101 up + 59 down = 160, P<0.01; Supp Table S4)
SCA vs CON at baseline, secondary/non-exercise (S3.p1; paper: 2264 genes, FDR<0.001 and +/-1.50 log2FC; Supp Table S1)
final.paper_method: limma-voom normalization of raw counts; limma linear models adjusted by sex with a group x time interaction term (limma v3.50.3) (S2.4.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.3.p1 gives assay and GSE244401; S2.4.p1 gives limma-voom, sex adjustment, interaction term, P<0.01 for exercise effects and FDR<0.001 for baseline; S3.p1 gives the DEG counts; TAB1 gives 23 SCA (11M/12F) and 17 CON (12M/5F). The paper does not state whether pairing was modelled (subject block, duplicateCorrelation, or none).

checks: GEO contact Abel Plaza-Florido, UC Irvine PERC = paper group
80 samples = 40 participants x 2 time points; 23 SCA x2 = 46 and 17 CON x2 = 34 match TAB1
metadata sex counts per group (SCA 12F/11M, CON 5F/12M) match TAB1
data_processing: HISAT2 + featureCounts raw counts matches S2.3.p1

ownership.reasoning: The series is the paper's own deposit and its sample set matches the paper's included participants exactly.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns equal metadata title (80/80, inspect alignment_keys). subject = participant code from title (CON02, SCA01, ...); T1/T2 suffix agrees with characteristics 'time 1'/'time 2'; time 1 = baseline (before CIIT), time 2 = immediately after (S2.3.p1).

matrix.reasoning: integer fraction 1.0, max 2.1e7, Ensembl gene IDs, 60675 features; GEO data_processing and S2.3.p1 both say featureCounts raw counts.

design.subject: subject

final.analysis_type: repeated-measures 2x2 (group between subjects x time within subjects)
final.formula: paired change (post - pre per subject) ~ 0 + C(grp); baseline: ~ grp + sex on pre samples

design.reasoning: S1.p4/S2.4.p1: within-group post vs pre and the group x time interaction are the exercise estimands; baseline SCA vs CON is a disease (associational) comparison kept as secondary. Exercise intensity is not a factor because the authors pooled 50% and 70% (S2.4.p1, S4.p7). Post-exercise SCA vs CON is not a paper contrast and is not run.

candidates.value: intensity as a factor (moderate vs vigorous)
candidates.reason_rejected: paper pooled intensities (S2.4.p1); exploratory only in the paper with no reported result
pre and post samples come from the same child; ignoring the pairing misstates the variance of within-subject effects

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: paper adjusts by sex (S2.4.p1); constant within subject, so it cancels in the paired post-pre differences; included as a covariate in the baseline between-group model

covariance.reasoning: Each participant contributes a pre and a post sample, so the participant is the blocking unit for the exercise contrasts; it is handled by taking within-subject differences (paired change), equivalent to a subject fixed-effect model. Group and sex are between-subject and are not estimable alongside subject fixed effects, which is why the baseline comparison is fitted on pre samples only with sex as a covariate.

final.method: limma (log2(CPM+1), paired-change design) for exercise contrasts; limma ~ grp + sex on baseline samples
final.formula: delta_post_minus_pre ~ 0 + C(grp); contrasts C(grp)[SCA], C(grp)[CON], C(grp)[SCA]-C(grp)[CON]

paper_route.method: limma-voom with sex-adjusted group x time interaction model
paper_route.reason: tools/limma_voom_tools.py:60 run_limma_voom_analysis is two-group only (no covariates, no blocking, no interaction); the multi-factor limma executor (tools/multigroup_tools.py) fits limma on a log-scale matrix without voom precision weights

deviations: log2(CPM+1) (preprocess_counts, low-expression filter) + ordinary limma instead of voom precision weights
pairing modelled explicitly by within-subject differences; the paper does not state its pairing model
sex adjustment omitted from the paired exercise contrasts because sex is constant within subject and cancels

method.reasoning: Raw counts allow voom, but no executor combines voom with blocking/interaction; the validated alternative is limma on log-CPM with the paired-change plan. DESeq2 paired within-group fits (~ subject + time) and unpaired limma-voom within-group fits run as sensitivity checks on the raw counts.

final.deviation_note: Exercise rule P<0.01 with no fold-change cutoff (S2.4.p1, S3.p1 'FC ranged from ...' is descriptive). The baseline table has a different paper rule (FDR<0.001, +/-1.50 log2FC); its count under that rule is computed from the result table and reported separately; the applied P<0.01 count for baseline is not comparable.

threshold.reasoning: S2.4.p1: 'P-value cut-off of 0.01 for exercise effects on gene expression'; audit rule BH padj<0.05 shown for reference.

caveats: paper used voom weights; here log2(CPM+1) limma
paper's pairing model is not stated
raw P<0.01 thresholds over ~20k genes carry many expected false positives (~200 per contrast)

study.reasoning: S3.p1 counts; S4.p3 and S4.p5 named genes.

discrepancies.data: every participant has a pre and post sample (40 complete pairs)

executions.reasoning: One limma fit on the 40 within-subject post-pre differences; group means give the within-group exercise effects and their difference gives the group x time interaction (S2.4.p1).

executions.name: baseline_SCA_vs_CON
